questions.question: What time do the records give for the arrival at Kestrelune Arcade?
questions.expected_answer: The arrival observation estimates near 09:26 on April 18, 2034. The follow-up says this was reconstructed from planned bells, not a checked clock; it does not establish a parcel delivery time.

questions.question: When does the dispatch observation place departure?
questions.expected_answer: 09:14 on April 18, 2034 according to the unchecked wall clock; the observer did not read the band number.

questions.question: Can the later clock comparison correct the dispatch time?
questions.expected_answer: No. The April 19 comparison found the clock seven minutes slow but does not establish its April 18 offset.

questions.question: What bell times were planned and were they observed arrival times?
questions.expected_answer: 09:10, 09:25 and 09:40 on April 18 were planned bells. The first bell was delayed; those are not observed arrival times.

questions.question: When was the screen moved?
questions.expected_answer: The account says after the third rehearsal bell; no exact time is identified and the bell delay was not measured.

questions.question: On what date was the follow-up count recorded?
questions.expected_answer: April 19, 2034. It recorded eleven visible cases at the storehouse, one empty case at the arcade and a sealed parcel behind a screen; its contents were not inspected.
